key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (at least 5% and at least 2% more than placebo) were somnolence and sedation (16% vs 8% placebo), dizziness (12% vs 7%), fatigue (9% vs 4%), and nausea/vomiting (5% vs 3%). Discontinuation due to adverse events was 5%, 8%, and 7% at 50/100/200 mg/day vs 4% for placebo. Labeled warnings include suicidal behavior and ideation, neurological (somnolence/fatigue, dizziness/gait) reactions, psychiatric reactions (13% vs 8% placebo), and hypersensitivity (bronchospasm/angioedema).

The discontinuation rates due to adverse events were 5%, 8%, and 7% for patients randomized to receive BRIVIACT at the recommended doses of 50 mg, 100 mg, and 200 mg/day, respectively, compared to 4% in patients randomized to receive placebo.

BRIVIAC causes psychiatric adverse reactions. In the Phase 3 controlled adjunctive epilepsy trials, psychiatric adverse reactions were reported in approximately 13% of patients who received BRIVIAC (at least 50 mg/day) compared to 8% of patients who received placebo.

BRIVIAC causes dose-dependent increases in somnolence and fatigue-related adverse reactions (fatigue, asthenia, malaise, hypersomnia, sedation, and lethargy) [see *Adverse Reactions* (6.1)]. In the Phase 3 controlled adjunctive epilepsy trials, these events were reported in 25% of patients randomized to receive BRIVIAC at least 50 mg/day (20% at 50 mg/day, 26% at 100 mg/day, and 27% at 200 mg/day)

BRIVIAC causes adverse reactions related to dizziness and disturbance in gait and coordination (dizziness, vertigo, balance disorder, ataxia, nystagmus, gait disturbance, and abnormal coordination) [see *Adverse Reactions* (6.1)]. BRIVIAC can cause hypersensitivity reactions. Bronchospasm and angioedema have been reported in patients taking BRIVIAC. If a patient develops hypersensitivity reactions after treatment with BRIVIAC, the drug should be discontinued. BRIVIAC is contraindicated in patients with a prior hypersensitivity reaction to brivaracetam or any of the inactive ingredients [see *Contraindications* (4)].
